claims.text: Cast NbMoTaW-V or NbMoTaTiW alloys have a coarse-grained, single-phase BCC initial structure.
NbMoTaW and NbMoTaWV refractory multi-principal element alloys have limited room-temperature ductility.
The cast baseline has yield strength below 1000 MPa.
High-pressure torsion or cryogenic rolling can refine the proposed refractory alloy to a grain size below 50 nm.
A sub-solvus anneal after severe plastic deformation can produce a dual BCC/B2 structure in the proposed refractory alloy.
Annealing at 0.4–0.6 Tm for less than one hour in argon will avoid grain coarsening and unwanted intermetallic precipitation.
The resulting B2 precipitates will be nanoscale and coherent or semi-coherent with the BCC matrix.
High configurational entropy and limited diffusion during the short anneal stabilize the BCC/B2 nanostructure.
Severe plastic deformation increases dislocation density and grain-boundary area, which provide nucleation sites for B2.
Lower-temperature annealing can drive decomposition into ordered B2 and disordered BCC phases, with the decomposition length scale controlled by composition and annealing temperature.
A short anneal permits B2 formation without sufficient time for coarse Laves or other brittle intermetallic phases to form.
An atomic-size mismatch below 6.6% is an empirical condition favoring BCC solid-solution formation in high-entropy alloys.
A valence electron concentration of at least 4.6 is empirically associated with brittle high-entropy alloys.
Maintaining VEC below 4.6 and atomic-size mismatch below 6.6% suppresses brittle intermetallics while stabilizing B2 in a BCC matrix.
Exceeding either VEC 4.6 or atomic-size mismatch 6.6% favors Laves or complex tetragonal phases over the desired BCC/B2 structure.
The proposed nanocrystalline BCC/B2 material will have yield strength above 2000 MPa and ductility above 10%.
The proposed material will have hardness above 600 Hv.
Ductility above 10% will result from suppressing brittle intermetallic networks and retaining a ductile BCC matrix.

contradictions.description: The boundary predicts that alloys above VEC 4.6 or δ 6.6% should fail to form BCC/B2 and instead form brittle phases, but the falsification rule incorrectly labels that predicted result as falsification rather than confirmation.

The hypothesis requires grain sizes below 50 nm, whereas the falsification rule only treats coarsening above 100 nm as failure, leaving outcomes between 50 and 100 nm inconsistent with the target but not falsifying.
